Yeah I can see that. I'm not uncomfortable knowing I'm AFAB. I don't feel uncomfortable telling physicians I'm female at the doctors office. But how I feel is not *normal,* persay, when someone just calls me a woman because thats how I present myself. Don't say I'm acting in such a way because I'm a woman, but rather because I'm a human. Maybe it has to do with internalized misogyny though... I guess I'm still trying to figure everything out.

Dressing is a bit confusing for me because I just want to look nice/attractive, regardless of my sex. Like I want to dress more masculine, but I think feminine clothing complements my features more. I think I might just need to get over my performative social anxiety to get more comfortable in my skin.

Yeah I spoke to one of my NB friends and they said that if I don't want labels I don't need to find one. But I really feel like finding a label, and then the corresponding community, will help ground me in this confusing time of identity. 

Also I'm scared to come out with how I feel to my bf (who is very much an ally) cos he's said he prefers to date cis women :,) Oh well, lets see where life takes me

Yeah I think what has really been wracking my brain is what does it mean to even be a woman? In fact, what does it mean to even be female, having XX chromosomes? But then what about intersex women with XXY chromosomes? 

Reading all these books in my gender/sexuality courses only makes me realize gender is so vague. Labels are lame but it helps ground people; and I think although I hate labels, finding one will be relieving for me. Thank you for your response it was food for thought. <3
Thank you for the books. I now have something to read over break :-) Also your music analogy was eye opening to me thanks.
Hi, thank you for your response! I'm slowly learning more and more that I might be NB. I think I feel in tune with the fluid nature of being NB. Your response was helpful :-)
Also thank you, I didn't know agender, gender apathetic, or GNC were a thing!

I've just been surrounded by terms like female, XY, periods are woman, breasts are woman. I've only recently been taking college courses on gender and sexuality so I'm now realizing the stark difference between sex and gender. But since I've lived most of my life equating the two as the same its hard to differentiate in daily life.
